item.title: BridgeBio Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Drug
item.description:
• Summary: The FDA has accepted BridgeBio's application for its investigational gene therapy, BBP-418 (also known as LAM-107), for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9). This is a potential first-ever approved treatment for the condition, which is caused by mutations in the FKRP gene. The acceptance sets a PDUFA date for a decision. BridgeBio's therapy aims to restore functional FKRP protein expression, addressing the underlying genetic defect. LGMD is a progressive muscle-wasting disease with no approved disease-modifying therapies.
  • MoAs: Gene therapy delivering a functional copy of the FKRP gene via an adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector to restore glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan, stabilizing muscle cell membranes.
  • Sources: BioSpace
